items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: So I met him. And then around the same time I got a call from Woody Herman... while I was in New York a call was sent from L.A. back there to me from Benny Goodman. And I subsequently went to a rehearsal of his

ctx.x: Had you done much improvising before that?

A little bit. I liked Benny Goodman when I was playing the clarinet and my neighbor across the street played the drums. And we’d get together and do Benny Goodman and Gene Krupa, just the two of us. So I had a little bit, but I didn’t have, at that point I had just started studying harmony. In high school I started studying harmony. And that turned into a many year study that I spent a lot of time studying in different — starting from scratch twice, three times actually, and so I got a pretty thorough foundation…
Yeah. So if you saw E minor seven in your chart, you kind of knew what to do with that.
